items.title: Noah Okafor at the double as Leeds hit back to demolish sorry Chelsea
items.summary:
Xabi Alonso is straying towards crisis territory. Here’s a mind-bending statistic: Chelsea are eighth but have now lost more league games than Manchester United. They were bullied by a rampant Leeds, who fully merited their first win at Stamford Bridge since returning to the top of the table with a 2-0 victory in December 1999, and can look forward to another season with no European football if they do not sharpen up soon.

It is not really worth dwelling on the fact that the second Leeds goal, a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty early in a one-sided second half, came after Morgan Rogers was harshly penalised for handball. That was a minor detail given the wider picture. Leeds, superbly coached by Daniel Farke and up to sixth after two clinical strikes from Noah Okafor, Calvert-Lewin’s sixth goal of the season and a late effort from Brenden Aaronson, were so dominant that it was easy to conclude they would have won even without a helping hand from the officials.

items.title: Coventry edge thriller to keep Crystal Palace bottom and ruin Thomas Frank’s start
items.summary:
Twice Crystal Palace equalised. They seemed to have stabilised after half-time. But when the momentum is against you, sometimes even a change of manager cannot stop the rot. With five minutes remaining, a long throw arced into the box. Brandon Thomas-Asante headed it goalwards. Dean Henderson got in the way but the ball bounced off him, hit Dwight McNeil and ricocheted in. Palace may feel themselves unlucky, but Thomas Frank started with a defeat and his side have now lost five successive league games.

For much of the second half, there had been reasons for Palace optimism. They seemed to have settled better after a ludicrous first half in which neither side looked at all capable of defending. But a triple substitution by Frank Lampard with 20 minutes to go shifted the game back in Coventry’s favour for a win that lifted them three points clear of the relegation zone.

Continue reading...
items.t: Coventry edge thriller to keep Crystal Palace bottom and ruin Thomas Frank’s start

items.title: Fading Beauden Barrett a symbol of rabble All Blacks’ joyless decline | Gerard Meagher
items.summary:
Storied full-back’s celebration turns to ash and New Zealand risk more than Rennie’s wrath if they don’t bounce back soon

If their punishment last week was to be told in no uncertain terms that they had let the country down, what awaits the All Blacks after this? Public humiliation? Exile? A firing squad at dawn? That New Zealand followed head coach Dave Rennie’s rebuke with their worst Twickenham performance of the professional era and a record defeat by England suggests such criticism monumentally backfired.

Perhaps it is wise to remember it is only a game, Dave. For what made the very best All Blacks sides so impressive was that they always looked like they were having fun. That they would showcase the most mesmerising skills and do so with a smile on their faces took the breath away and added to the allure. This rabble did not look like they were having much fun out there.

Continue reading...

items.title: Carlos Alcaraz holds off Ben Shelton to book place in ATP Finals
items.summary:
• Winner claims 3-6, 6-3, 7-6 (1) victory in semi-final

  • Second seed beats American after sensational 7-1 tie-break

The man himself was not present in Turin on Saturday afternoon, but one of the most intriguing developments on and off court in men’s tennis this year was Ben Shelton’s surprise decision to hire the former No 1 Juan-Carlos Ferrero as his new coach alongside his father, Bryan. Ferrero is one of the most highly respected coaches on tour, but he also knows Carlos Alcaraz better than any other coach in the world.

However, there is only so much that anyone can do against one of this sport’s greatest talents. Shelton, the third seed, played a spectacular match, serving monstrously, attacking without hesitation and particularly volleying so well in decisive moments, but it still wasn’t enough to defeat the second seeded Alcaraz, who maintained his focus after an uncertain start as he reached the final of the ATP Finals with a 3-6, 6-3, 7-6 (1) win over Shelton.

items.title: Slade helps sparkling England power to record victory as All Blacks wilt again
items.summary:
• England 37-12 New Zealand

  • Slade scores the first of five tries for England

Every year the All Blacks come to south-west London it feels like an acid test. And rarely, if ever, have England responded with such class and conviction on this famous old stretch of grass. New Zealand simply could not live with their clear-eyed, motivated opponents who, at times, made their illustrious visitors look horribly second-rate.

If Kiwi fans thought last week’s loss to Wales was painful this was arguably as bad in terms of the reputational damage. The home side were 19-0 up after 36 minutes and had the game all but wrapped up within a couple of minutes of the restart when Ollie Chessum smashed his way over to claim his side’s fourth try. From a margin of victory perspective this was England’s biggest over New Zealand in the 121-year-old history of the fixture.

Consider the training regime Dele Alli has followed since he left Como 18 months ago and it becomes clear why he takes exception to suggestions he has given up on football in favour of becoming an internet personality.

He trains five or six days a week with Connor Peters, an elite performance coach who has worked with players including Trevoh Chalobah. They spend four days on the pitch and days in between in the gym. A typical day begins at 9am with an hour of activation and stretching before Dele heads to non-league Windsor & Eton at 11am, where he trains on the pitches and uses the facilities. Then it’s back home to use his own oxygen chamber and sauna for a recovery session.

items.title: Men’s tennis boosts prize money for players to more than $350m in major overhaul
items.summary:
• Cash increase via ATP’s creation of ‘One Vision’ company

  • More rest breaks added to reduce player welfare issues

The Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) has approved major changes to the financial structure of men’s tennis that will make the total prize money available to the players increase to more than $350m (£267m) by 2028, from $270m this year.

The creation of a new company to sell all the tour’s media, commercial and data rights, ATP Ventures, will lead to the investment of an additional $100m in player remuneration including an increased $50m bonus pool, a $25m year-end rankings bonus and $26m player pensions.
